lines: the drive knows where the rotor is from the first instant, so it applies only the current the torque needs
Power stage: a three-phase inverter, 6 switches.

Current: 12.1 A peak at the design point, 12.1 A holding the same torque at standstill. Start with devices rated for 24.2 A or more: the rating on a datasheet's first page assumes a case held at 25 °C, which no real heatsink does.
Voltage: 60 V parts are the least that keeps a 48 V supply under 80% of the rating. 80 V parts leave room for switching overshoot and for the link voltage rising when the motor brakes.

Technology: silicon MOSFETs are the usual choice at this voltage. GaN transistors are worth a look when switching above about 100 kHz or when board area decides: they lose less per switching event and take less space.
On-resistance: about 10 mΩ or less when hot keeps conduction loss near 1% of the motor's power; that is about 5.56 mΩ on the datasheet's 25 °C line.
Packaging: discrete MOSFETs with a gate-driver IC (3 half-bridge channels, bootstrap supplies for the high side), or a driver with the MOSFETs built in at a few amps.
